summary: Lesotho’s pledges mix restoration, conservation and agriculture. The headline restoration target is to increase planted forests by 61,325 ha by 2030 relative to 2015—equivalent to about 15.5% of current mapped forest area (3,953 km²); a separate 5% forest-cover formulation equals about 1,533 km², while forest already covers 12.9% of land. Conservation and mixed measures include rehabilitating 30 pilot wetlands, implementing 18 of 74 catchment plans, cutting traditional biomass use to under 5%, and deploying 9,030 efficient stoves unconditionally or 30,800 conditionally by 2030. Agriculture targets include 20% of productive land under conservation agriculture, 60% more livestock under improved management, a 20% increase in farmer access to resilient seed, 80% more improved crop technologies, 15% more households fitted with rainwater harvesting and 100% of rural institutions. The mixed AFOLU pledge seeks a 6% unconditional reduction and another conditional 6% by 2030.
